correctness.rationale: At fixed n and k the integer coefficient row is the law after division by binom(n,k), including the point mass at zero for k=0,1. A spanning subtree includes an edge iff the chosen leaves meet both cut sides; counting subsets gives the mean numerator and for k=2 the subtree length is pair distance. The full law determines both the mean vector and the two-tip raw second moment. The frozen leaf-insertion census is exhaustive by removing a leaf and suppressing its neighbor, and its center-rooted sorted signatures are complete for tree isomorphism. An independent replay instead enumerated by leaf-weighted centroids: an equal-half edge is unique when it exists and splits into an unordered pair of planted trees; otherwise orient edges toward the strictly greater side when it has more than half the leaves. Since every vertex has at most one outgoing edge and the graph is a tree, there is one sink, at which the three unordered planted branches each have fewer than half the leaves. Planted branches are generated by all unordered binary splits. For every shape through 14 the replay computed all subset laws by subtracting the common root-to-LCA path from the union of root-to-leaf paths, independently of the frozen cut method and without pruning by the moment signature. It recovered the census counts 1,1,1,2,2,4,6,11,18,37,66,135, distinct mean-plus-second-moment signatures through 13, and 132 moment classes but 134 full-law classes at 14. The three nontrivial moment classes are pairs; only one pair agrees in all coefficients. Both witness edge lists pass the tree and degree tests, have different centroid codes, and match precisely the full-law pair; the 69 terms give digest 39dd8ac22976f34cecc7184c4196f401cf3de782053cfc939bb17ff8f397759d.
residual_risks: The exhaustive certificate covers the finite class through 14 leaves only. The units and sampling assumptions are essential: the law is for uniform leaf subsets, not arclength sampling, arbitrary weights or a joint sequence.

evidence: The degree-(k+1) combinatorial-tree theorem includes degree-three unit-edge trees at k=2 but requires the joint probability distribution of the nested random length sequence. Other inspected work gives unrooted forward moments or statistics obtained by aggregating split sizes.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Broader results about the same tree class with richer data do not imply a reconstruction theorem from weaker data. Forward moment formulas and split-size aggregates do not establish injectivity or full-law collisions. The collision found here necessarily separates the full marginals from the joint law on this class.

evidence: In the ten-tip record a subset's statistic is the union of its root-to-tip paths; even a singleton contributes positive length. The sixteen-tip record's distinct two-tip frequencies rule out equality of its full laws despite matching two moments. Evans–Lanoue use one uniform listing to produce nested samples.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The rooted union includes a path above the sampled tips' common ancestor that is excluded in the unrooted span. A failure at a single depth, or even at all depths separately with possibly different pairs, does not give one pair matching every marginal. Equality of lower moments is necessary but cannot establish equality of laws; joint injectivity also does not supply marginal injectivity.

evidence: The Steiner Wiener index is a sum of Steiner distances over all k-subsets of vertices. The corresponding leaf-restricted sum is [z^k] of the u derivative of F_T at u=1. A potentially related Steiner-distance Hosoya polynomial source was identified but not retrieved in full.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: On trees, minimal subtree length is Steiner distance on the sampled terminals, so an all-k terminal-restricted histogram is indeed an equivalent formulation. The inspected Steiner index is not that histogram: it aggregates distances, and its usual domain is all vertices rather than original leaves. No collision threshold for the equivalent formulation was found in the checked text.

No inspected result implies the minimal unrooted all-marginal collision, its uniqueness at 14, or identification with a weaker mixed-moment statistic through 13. value.rationale: Separate rarefaction laws are a natural coarsening of the nested joint sampling law, and their information loss is not evident from the forward formulas. A unique smallest pair matching every marginal shows exactly where this form of reconstruction first breaks in the unit-edge binary class. The additional finite result through thirteen tips identifies how much less information is already sufficient there: the means plus one two-tip distance moment. The concrete witness and first obstruction are useful even without any assertion beyond fourteen tips.
residual_risks: The theorem is exact identifiability, not a finite-sample procedure, robustness result, or reconstruction theorem for weighted trees.
